baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative sequence قُلِ ... ٱلْحَمْدُ ... وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا frames the ayah as an enacted utterance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Speech externalizes praise, the three negations supply its grounds, and the doubled closing root turns recognition of greatness into the commanded culmination.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech makes the verse a performed proclamation rather than a silent inventory.
Praise opposed to blame gives the proclamation its evaluative center.
Rightful greatness and majesty make the verb-masdar close an emphatic act of exaltation.

changed_reading.before: The ayah lists divine attributes and appends praise.
changed_reading.after: The ayah commands a voiced verdict: convert the three negated dependencies into praise and emphatic magnification.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three coordinated لَمْ clauses deny a child, a partner in the dominion, and an ally arising from humiliation.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence closes three routes by which human rule is stabilized: acquired lineage, divided title, and protective patronage. Divine dominion is therefore not merely singular but structurally nondependent.

activation_trace.role: Acquisition for oneself casts taking a child as adding a support or possession.
Born offspring supplies the lineage relation explicitly excluded from divine identity.
Participation between multiple parties supplies the divided claim denied within dominion.
Sovereignty and rule define the field in which participation is excluded.
Taking charge of another's affair supplies the external support that God does not require.
Abasement under coercion states the deficit from which such protective support would arise.

changed_reading.before: The verse separately denies three associates of God.
changed_reading.after: The coordinated denials map one mechanism: sovereignty needing neither dynastic continuation, shared administration, nor rescue from weakness.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening context makes creatures dependent on divine guidance and unable to find protective allies apart from Him; the focus reverses the relation by denying that God Himself needs an ally because of abasement.

activation_trace.role: Gentle direction to the right way supplies the guidance on which the creature depends.
Supportive alliance names the rescuing relation creatures cannot secure elsewhere.
Otherness marks the failed search for a protector apart from God.
The same supportive alliance is denied as a relation God would need for Himself.
Coerced abasement identifies the deficiency that could necessitate a protector, then excludes it from God.

structural_cues: 17:97 denies finding allies apart from Him, while 17:111 denies an ally for Him arising from humiliation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored ally language and opposite dependency positions; I infer a protector/protected reversal, while a live alternative is that each clause only rejects false patrons locally.

changed_reading.after: God is the sought source of protection, not a vulnerable being whose sovereignty must be repaired by a protector.

context_deltas.mechanism: The resurrection challenge moves from disintegrated remains to new creation and then to cosmic creation and capacity. Against that display of origination, denying a child distinguishes sovereign creation from genealogical self-extension rather than suggesting an absence of generative power.

activation_trace.role: Something arising from another supplies the derivative-production possibility that the child clause excludes.
Innovative bringing-into-being supplies the challenged act of renewed creation.
New occurrence after rupture makes recreation follow bodily disintegration without lineage.
Repeated origination joins cosmic creation to the creation of beings like the challengers.
Effective capacity supplies the power by which origination reaches action.
Likeness supplies reproducible creatures without making them divine offspring.

structural_cues: 17:98 asks whether bones and fragments can become a new creation; 17:99 answers through creation of the heavens, earth, and beings like them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies derivative offspring, newness after rupture, origination, likeness, and effective capacity; I infer a contrast between genealogy and creation, while the narrower alternative is a denial of offspring with no theory of production implied.

changed_reading.before: The child clause is a bare denial of offspring.
changed_reading.after: The clause separates God's abundant power to originate and re-originate from the creaturely mechanism of deriving continuity through offspring.

context_deltas.mechanism: The hypothetical in 17:100 puts mercy's treasuries under human ownership and immediately yields hoarding from fear of depletion. The focus's unshared dominion then reads as freedom from scarcity-conditioned co-management: mercy is not exposed to a parsimonious partner's veto.

activation_trace.role: Sovereignty supplies the divine dominion whose mode is clarified by the human counterexample.
Possession and disposal place the imagined treasuries under human control.
Secured storage supplies the bounded-resource image that invites hoarding.
Merciful tenderness identifies what human ownership would constrict.
Miserly retention supplies the failed human administration of mercy.
Expenditure of wealth supplies the imagined loss that produces withholding.
Constriction and reduction diagnose the scarcity logic of human control.

structural_cues: 17:100 and 17:111 are both قُلْ declarations linking م ل ك to sharply different human and divine modes of rule.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a conditional chain from human ownership through fear of spending to constriction; I carry that chain into the focus's unshared dominion, while the alternative is that 17:100 criticizes humans without explaining why dominion has no partner.

changed_reading.after: Unshared dominion also means mercy cannot be rationed by a scarcity-bound co-owner who fears that giving will exhaust the store.

context_deltas.mechanism: The confrontation with Pharaoh culminates in an attempt to shake a people from the land, followed by the coercer's drowning, the people's settlement, and their later gathering as a mixed whole. The focus's unpartnered dominion becomes a verdict on coercive rule that cannot secure its own project.

activation_trace.role: Sovereignty supplies the focus anchor against which the preceding contest of rule is read.
Destabilizing lightness supplies the attempted removal of a people from their ground.
Caused drowning supplies the reversal that terminates the coercer's project.
Undivided completeness makes the reversal encompass the ruler and all with him.
Settled habitation reverses the attempted displacement.
A mixed collectivity gathered as one supplies the later reorganization of dispersed people.

structural_cues: 17:101-102 stage the confrontation with Pharaoh; 17:103-104 reverse attempted expulsion into drowning, settlement, and eventual gathering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies displacement, drowning, settlement, and gathering; I assign their reversal as evidence about sovereignty in 17:111, while they may instead remain historical acts without an institutional gloss.

changed_reading.before: The denial of a partner in dominion is an abstract exclusivity claim.
changed_reading.after: It also closes the Pharaoh sequence as a judgment that coercive possession of land is not a durable share in ultimate rule.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those given knowledge repeatedly fall, prostrate, and increase in humility. The upward semantic force of magnifying God is therefore paired with the knower's voluntary bodily lowering, sharply unlike the coerced humiliation denied of God.

activation_trace.role: Rightful greatness supplies the upward pole recognized by the final imperative.
Abasement under coercion marks the lowering explicitly excluded from God.
Audible, unsteady falling gives recognition of revelation a downward bodily vector.
Prostrating lowliness turns the fall into willing worship rather than defeat.
Increase and growth create the paradoxical upward measure of a deepening low posture.
Humble lowering names what grows as divine greatness is recognized.

structural_cues: يَخِرُّونَ is repeated in 17:107 and 17:109, and the upward verb يَزِيدُ takes خُشُوعًا as its result immediately before the repeated ك ب ر close.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated falling, prostration, increasing humility, and emphatic magnification; I infer a reciprocal vertical axis, while the alternative treats these as adjacent but independent devotional acts.

changed_reading.before: Magnifying God is chiefly an upward verbal assertion.
changed_reading.after: Magnification is tested by a reversal in the worshipper: recognition rises as the knowledgeable body and self voluntarily lower.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding instruction rejects both raised proclamation and inaudibility in prayer and commands a traversable middle way. Emphatic magnification in 17:111 therefore cannot be equated with maximizing acoustic force; it names the magnitude of recognition within a calibrated voice.

activation_trace.role: Deeming something great in the breast supplies semantic magnification without prescribing maximal loudness.
Public declaration and raised sound supply the upper vocal extreme explicitly barred.
Secret, lowered utterance supplies the opposite vocal extreme explicitly barred.
A state intermediate between two ends supplies the calibration principle.
A traversable extended path turns calibration into a sustained practice rather than a midpoint abstraction.

structural_cues: The two vocal prohibitions in 17:110 immediately precede 17:111's قُلِ and emphatic verb-masdar magnification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit vocal bounds followed by emphatic takbir; I infer that adjacency blocks a loudness reading, while the live alternative confines the bounds to prayer and leaves the next imperative acoustically unspecified.

changed_reading.before: كَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا may suggest making praise as loud or externally large as possible.
changed_reading.after: Magnify Him without mistaking decibels for greatness: emphatic recognition remains compatible with the measured vocal path just prescribed.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads metaphysical relation nouns through institutional supports of rule. It remains anchored in child, partner, dominion, ally, and the displacement-settlement reversal; downstream prose should present it as a political analogy, not the verse's exclusive referent or a historical identification.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: وَلَدًا, شَرِيكٌ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ, and وَلِىٌّ form three relation slots around explicit dominion.

activation_trace.role: Offspring supplies the dynastic-continuity slot in the analogy.
Multi-party participation supplies the co-regency slot in the analogy.
Sovereignty makes institutional rule an explicit rather than free-floating comparison.
Administrative guardianship supplies the patron or regent slot in the analogy.
Destabilization supplies the coercive sovereign practice whose durability is tested.
Settlement supplies the divine reversal of attempted territorial removal.

changed_reading.before: The three negations are only a list of metaphysical exclusions.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they also dismantle the familiar architecture of fragile regimes: dynasty, co-rule, and emergency patronage are all unnecessary to divine dominion.

strongest_changes: The 17:100 ownership counterfactual turns unshared dominion into freedom from scarcity-driven withholding of mercy.
The ally language in 17:97 reverses the dependency relation: creatures seek protection from God, whereas God needs no protector from abasement.
The 17:107-110 sequence calibrates takbir through voluntary lowering and a voice between loudness and inaudibility.
summary.what_was_special: Repeated focus roots and mirrored constructions made the context unusually diagnostic: م ل ك contrasts human and divine control, و ل ي reverses protector and protected, and the final ك ب ر imperative arrives after both bodily descent and vocal calibration.
remaining_uncertainties: The creation context strongly supports a creation-versus-genealogy contrast, but the derivative-production branch of و ل د remains broader than the ordinary offspring sense.
The political reading is structurally visible through explicit dominion and the Pharaoh reversal, but its institutional detail is analogical.
The prayer-volume rule may govern only 17:110 locally even though its adjacency sharply constrains a loudness reading of 17:111.
